People find websites through AI answers as often as search results now. A site that neither ranks on Google nor gets mentioned by AI assistants is invisible twice. A Self-growing Website works both fronts, on a schedule you approve. No content calendar, no agency.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a self-growing website?

A website that keeps growing after it goes live. Greta builds and publishes the site, then researches your site and the sources you pick, and suggests new articles, pages and fixes. Nothing goes live until it's approved, and once publishing is switched on, an approved schedule publishes new articles on its own. [...] ### How is that different from a normal website?

A normal website is finished the day it launches and starts going stale the day after. Keeping it current means a content calendar, an SEO agency, or remembering to update it yourself. A self-growing website brings you the next article or fix to approve instead.

### Does it help with AI search as well as Google?

Yes. Greta checks your titles, descriptions and structure so search engines can rank your pages, and checks that AI assistants like ChatGPT can read your site so they can mention it.

# Greta.sh vs Bolt.new: Which AI Builder Is Right for You in 2026?

Greta.sh vs Bolt.new: Which AI Builder Is Right for You in 2026?

> Bolt.new and Greta.sh both build full-stack apps from a prompt, but they aim at different users. Bolt is the stronger choice for developers who want an in-browser environment with framework control and token-based flexibility. Greta.sh is the better choice for founders who want to launch a product without touching code — and have it grow itself, with SEO/AEO built in.

## Greta.sh vs Bolt at a glance [...] ## Where Greta.sh wins

Bolt suits people who are comfortable working in the code. Greta.sh assumes the opposite: that your goal is a live product with customers, and that you'd rather not manage a stack at all. So Greta.sh handles the build end-to-end from plain English and keeps working after launch, suggesting SEO and AI-search articles and fixes and publishing them on a schedule you approve. For a founder whose bottleneck is traction, not code, that post-launch growth layer is the whole point.
